## Captured excerpt

The source frames RAG as an LLM paired with an external searchable knowledge base and outlines a minimal pipeline based on chunking, embeddings, vector search, and prompt-time retrieval. It then argues that high-performing RAG requires much more than the simple baseline and highlights five refinement areas:
- hybrid search
- data cleaning and preprocessing
- prompt engineering
- evaluation
- data collection for improvement

## Initial relevance note
This source is useful for the pilot because it gives a practical view of what real RAG involves and therefore helps distinguish a knowledge compiler from a retrieval pipeline. It is especially useful as a comparison source rather than as a direct architectural template.
